description:
request.rs:86 — Ok(JmapRequest::new(self.using, self.method_calls, None))

JmapRequestBuilder::build() calls jmap_types::JmapRequest::new(_, _, None). This commits the base-client crate to whatever signature jmap-types::JmapRequest::new has, including its current `None` 3rd parameter.

If jmap-types adds a 4th parameter to JmapRequest::new (e.g., a request-level timeout, a "created" id-allocator slot), this crate breaks at compile time, ripples to every consumer.

This is normal workspace-internal coupling. The workspace AGENTS.md propagation policy documents this: changes to jmap-types ripple. Not a bug in this crate per se.

Two small notes:
1. The `None` 3rd argument is presumably the optional "createdIds" map (RFC 8620 §5.2). The doc-comment on JmapRequestBuilder::build doesn't mention that the builder hardcodes None — so a caller who wants to use createdIds-mediated request batching cannot do so via this builder. They'd have to construct JmapRequest::new themselves and bypass the builder.

2. If jmap-types stabilizes JmapRequest::new at 1.0, this crate can pin its dependency at 1.x and stay buildable. Today both are 0.x.

Recommendation: add a builder method `JmapRequestBuilder::with_created_ids(mut self, map: HashMap<...>) -> Self` so callers can use the createdIds feature without bypassing the builder. Low priority because RFC 8620 §5.2 createdIds is rarely used in practice (most clients don't batch dependent creates this way).
title: JmapRequest is constructed via JmapRequest::new from jmap-types — request.rs:86 commits to that constructor
